rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for surrounding a place with armed forces to force surrender.

example.english: The enemy forces besiege the city, and after holding out for several days, the defenders finally surrender.
example.traditional: 敵軍圍攻座城，守軍捱咗幾日終於投降。
example.jyutping: dik6 gwan1 wai4 gung1 zo6 sing4 sau2 gwan1 ngaai4 zo2 gei2 jat6 zung1 jyu1 tau4 hong4

rows.note: Use this when a person or problem persistently pesters or beleaguers someone rather than physically attacking a place.

example.english: Those troublesome customers constantly besiege me, leaving me no time to work.
example.traditional: 啲麻煩客成日纏住我，搞到我冇時間做嘢。
example.jyutping: di1 maa4 faan4 haak3 seng4 jat6 cin4 zyu6 ngo5 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 mou5 si4 gaan3 zou6 je5

rows.traditional: 追住 + A + 要求 + N/V
rows.jyutping: zeoi1 zyu6 A jiu1 kau4 N V
rows.note: Use this when people keep pressing A with demands or requests.

example.english: The customers besiege me with demands for a refund, leaving me no chance to take a break.
example.traditional: 班客追住我要求退款，搞到我冇得停低。
example.jyutping: baan1 haak3 zeoi1 zyu6 ngo5 jiu1 kau4 teoi3 fun2 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 mou5 dak1 ting4 dai1
